prompt: Dark editorial studio photography, depicting an old master craftsman seated at a wooden workbench in the act of making a delicate object, but both of the craftsman's hands have been replaced by precision measuring instruments: calipers, rulers, gauge needles, and micrometer jaws integrated where fingers should be. The tools are perfectly aligned, immaculate, and obsessively calibrated, yet they cannot actually grip, shape, or create the unfinished object lying on the bench. Around the workbench, every surface is covered with exact measurements, alignment rigs, and polished measuring devices, while the object being made remains inert, incomplete, and unloved. The scene should feel inevitable rather than fantastical: physically convincing, quiet, and deeply wrong. Composition: tight three-quarter view, the measuring hands dominating the foreground, the failed object clearly visible in the center. Mood: sterile obsession, loss of purpose through perfect measurement. Color palette: charcoal black, aged wood brown, steel silver, one dull amber task light. No text, no numbers, no charts, no labels, no mathematical notation, no formulas, no graphs, no target symbols, no literal dashboard or speedometer imagery, no infographic style.
visual_logic: A craftsman replaced by measuring instruments can optimize precision perfectly but cannot make the object; the metric has consumed the purpose it was meant to serve.
